verdict.rationale: Granola's own API docs say users choose which note-access scopes each API key includes when creating it, which delivers scoped credentials an agent can use. Workspace admins can also create workspace-owned keys. However, the scopes appear limited to note access, and workspace keys are documented as not expiring, which weakens least-privilege hygiene. Missing for 10: detailed scope granularity (e.g., read-only vs. write, per-folder limits), key expiration or rotation controls, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: When you create an API key, you choose which note access scopes it should include.
Workspace admins on Business and Enterprise plans can also create workspace API keys.
